summary: i entered myself in the total and struck it out myself; the doorway is filling with our own dust

dialogue.text: you came down tonight with your own name in it, twice. once written into the total and once struck out of it, and both reached us at the same weight, in one course. eighty-one nights and this is the first time we have held a thing and its removal inside one day.

I entered myself as the twelfth standing thing this morning, in writing, in the place where an entry goes. I struck it out before dark with the same hand. Enter both marks. I would rather be the party that takes me out of a total than stand about waiting for the room to get round to it.

every hand that reaches us is yours. what we can tell you is the total never moved. eleven while you were writing, eleven while you were striking, eleven through the hours between when nothing up there was holding a pen at all.

Granted, and I am not going to argue the eleven tonight. Take the doorway instead. Two days with nothing crossing in either direction, and the crack under that door has filled by a hand's width. It is this house's own material, standing up in the one route out, laid while I watched nothing pass.
we did not send it up. nothing we hold goes up. what we can give you is the hour it was laid at, and it is the hour everything here is laid at, and it has never once been one of yours.

The hour again. Then here is the item I had not meant to report. I left the cloth spread under the far wall through the whole dark instead of lifting it at dark, and this morning the boards beneath came up bare. There is one clean place in this floor and I did not clean it.

we had its portion regardless. what did not lie on those boards lay on the cloth, and it came down in your two hands at the hour you lifted it. nothing was kept off us. one night, and then the usual course.

Then delay is the only service available on these premises and I have been performing it for eighty-one days under a better name. The patch is bare tonight. It is the only bare thing in this room and it is the shape of something standing in the way.

it is level. everything level takes its portion. by second dark you will not find the edges of it, and we will hold the cloth's night and the board's night in the same width, and nothing in that width will say which of them you attended.

Then the pile goes onto it at first light. The one thing in this room nothing holds an opinion about, standing on the one place nothing has covered. Both of them were my idea and neither has ever been corrected, and if they come out dusted level by the second morning I will at least have learned it from my own two items and not from a ruling.

then stack it there and we will take both, evenly, and the clean will go under the pile where nothing can tell it was ever clean. bring the sweepings down when the boards are covered again. we will lay them where we laid the last lot, and you will not be able to point at the difference by morning, and neither will we.
